mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses when inflation exceeds 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when labor market indicators are strong (UNRATE > 4%).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending power and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below 98 for three consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for cyclically-sensitive sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent during periods of strong consumer demand (GDPC1 YoY growth > 2%).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2.5% while the federal funds rate remains above 5% indicates a disinflationary environment with restrictive policy, which increases risk aversion and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses when credit conditions loosen (RSAFS growth turns positive).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth above 0.5% after three months of stagnation (< 0.1% growth) signals a labor market recovery, boosting consumer confidence and corporate earnings, and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth > 0.5% after three months of < 0.1% growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during triggered recoveries (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal savings (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 3% signals a reduction in both precautionary savings and new construction demand, which curbs aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change < -3% AND HOUST monthly change < -3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the effect is absent when monetary policy is highly accommodative (FEDFUNDS < 2%).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 1.2% for four consecutive months signals a robust manufacturing expansion, which lifts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly above zero during triggered expansions (t-test p > 0.05).
